findings.evidence: Only `.source` is proved: `theorem symOpenPartialHomeomorph_source` at line 92; nothing else mentions the definition except `symChartAt_description`. Mathlib supplies the needed inputs: `mathlib/Mathlib/Topology/OpenPartialHomeomorph/Basic.lean:228 lemma toOpenPartialHomeomorph_left_inv`. The sibling homeomorphism in this development does provide them: `TauCeti/Analysis/Polynomial/SymmetricPower.lean:172 @[simp] coeffHomeomorph_apply`, `:177 coeffHomeomorph_symm_apply`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] symOpenPartialHomeomorph_apply : symOpenPartialHomeomorph c V m hm .. e hp (Sym.sumSubtype V m hm p) = piFinSumHomeomorph K e (fun i => Sym.coeffEquiv K (m i) (Sym.map (fun x : ↥(V i) => chartAt K (c i) (x : α)) (p i)))`, the corresponding `_symm_apply`, and `_target`. The proofs are `OpenPartialHomeomorph.trans_apply` plus `IsOpenEmbedding.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_left_inv` / `_apply`.
findings.issue: `symOpenPartialHomeomorph` is exposed with only `symOpenPartialHomeomorph_source` (line 92). There is no `_apply`, `_symm_apply` or `_target`, so no consumer can evaluate the chart or its inverse without unfolding the `letI`/`let` chain of the definition. Since `symChartAt` is `Exists.choose` and `symChartAt_description` (line 150) reduces it to exactly this definition, the whole charted structure is unusable for the stated next step (holomorphic transition maps `chart₂ ∘ chart₁.symm`).

findings.evidence: `noncomputable abbrev symChartSupport (s : Sym α n) : Finset α := by classical; exact (s : Multiset α).toFinset` (lines 104-106); the proof of `exists_openPartialHomeomorph_sym` must `unfold symChartSupport` (line 123) because no lemma relates it to `s`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem mem_symChartSupport {a : α} {s : Sym α n} : a ∈ symChartSupport s ↔ a ∈ s`, and state the definition as a plain `def` with the classical instance written out rather than a tactic block, so the intended `Finset` is unambiguous.
findings.issue: `symChartSupport` is public (it appears in the statements of `exists_openPartialHomeomorph_sym` and `symChartAt_description` as the index type `↥(symChartSupport s)`) but has no characteristic lemma: nothing states `a ∈ symChartSupport s ↔ a ∈ s`. Its body is a `by classical; exact` block, so the `DecidableEq` instance in `Multiset.toFinset` is `Classical.decEq`, which is not defeq to a user's own instance — a consumer cannot even reconstruct the index type by writing `(s : Multiset α).toFinset` themselves.

findings.evidence: `TauCeti/Topology/Sym/Basic.lean:181 instance instT2Space [T2Space α] : T2Space (Sym α n)`, reachable via `public import TauCeti.Topology.Sym.Family` → `TauCeti.Topology.Sym.Basic`; the file's variable line 58 has `[T2Space α]`.
findings.fix: Drop the Hausdorff clause from the docstring (or state that it is supplied by `TauCeti.Sym.instT2Space`), keeping only the second-countability caveat.
findings.issue: The `symChartedSpace` docstring says reading the result as a topological manifold "requires the separate Hausdorff instance on the symmetric power … which are not assumed here". `T2Space (Sym α n)` is already an instance in this file's import closure and the file assumes `[T2Space α]`, so it is automatic; only the countability clause is genuinely missing.

summary: The obsolete `appendSubtype` surface is fully removed and the `sumSubtype`/`piCurry` layers are well characterized, but the chart layer is opaque: `symOpenPartialHomeomorph` ships only a `_source` lemma, with no way to evaluate the chart or its inverse, and `symChartSupport` has no membership lemma. One docstring claim about the missing Hausdorff instance is false.
